details: Bitcoin has lost approximately half its value since its October 2025 peak of over $126,000, sliding to prices not seen since September 2024. This downturn is characterized by a "slow bleed" due to eroded investor interest and macro headwinds, rather than specific scandals or liquidations. Trading below its 200-week moving average, institutional investors show nervousness as rising oil prices reignite inflation concerns, creating a challenging environment for risk assets.
title: Bitcoin's Slump Differs From Past Selloffs, Enters "Slow Bleed"

details: Ondo Finance has expanded its 24/7 tokenized stock offerings to 16 assets, enabling continuous minting and redemption. Simultaneously, a partnership with Japan's SBI Group aims to tokenize Japanese equities and other assets, utilizing SBI's yen-backed stablecoin for settlement. These moves reinforce Ondo's lead in tokenized finance and its integration with traditional financial systems.
title: Ondo Boosts Tokenized Stocks, Partners With SBI for Japan Expansion

details: FTX announced it will start distributing approximately $900 million to creditors by the end of July. This marks the fifth round of payouts from the bankrupt crypto exchange, bringing the total distributed by its estate to nearly $10 billion since repayments began in 2025.
title: FTX to Begin $900M Payout to Creditors in Fifth Distribution Wave

details: Cardano (ADA) experienced a 3.5% drop in the last 16 hours due to traders repositioning ahead of the imminent Van Rossem hard fork, scheduled for July 18. This is compounded by a mildly risk-off broader crypto market and negative DeFi-ecosystem headlines. Despite the upgrade aiming to lower smart contract costs, increased short positions and a negative funding rate indicate cautious market sentiment.
title: Cardano (ADA) Drops Ahead of Van Rossem Hard Fork Amid Market Caution

details: Morgan Stanley's E*Trade platform has completed the rollout of spot Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana trading to its U.S. clients. The platform offers a competitive 50-basis-point fee, undercutting rivals like Coinbase and Robinhood. This move by one of Wall Street's largest wealth managers provides increased retail access to major digital assets.
title: Morgan Stanley's E*Trade Rolls Out Spot Crypto Trading to US Clients
